selectionBasis: All 28 current hold-editorial rows from the 48-row user-rule reassessment not in the two current replacement ten-lesson proposal batches (including its 14 still-unproposed teachable candidates), then the next 52 current held rows in source-ordinal order excluding those 28 and the two current proposal batches. Superseded proposal files are not treated as selected or as exclusions. No decision or selected manifest is changed.
guardrails: A candidate is not a selected lesson or approved alias.
An exclusion candidate is restricted to the exact one-time comparison and needs separate disposition review; ordinary reusable language is not excluded by default.
A selected-owner alias candidate requires the exact source sense and target span to match; broader owner forms need reviewed edits.
Concrete source defects stay held rather than being silently rewritten.

rows.exactGuideSentence: A simple line can land a punch in the final verse.
rows.guideMeaning: Have a strong impact; a fixed boxing metaphor.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The verse line has a strong figurative impact; the boxing phrase can transfer to speeches, headlines and jokes.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Keep the impact sense distinct from literal boxing and check natural determiner use.

rows.expression: the body was made to move
rows.exactGuideSentence: Even gentle walks remind us the body was made to move.
rows.guideMeaning: A memorable natural statement supporting regular activity; a natural spoken way to qualify or connect ideas.
rows.candidateTarget: the body was made to move
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The health claim uses the productive be made to + verb purpose frame rather than a one-off simile.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Teach it as a qualified activity claim, not a biological proof that every activity is safe.

rows.expression: move wisely than to push recklessly
rows.exactGuideSentence: After the injury, she learned it was better to move wisely than to push recklessly.
rows.guideMeaning: Choose safe activity over excessive effort; a balanced contrast.
rows.candidateTarget: better to move wisely than to push recklessly
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The source sentence contains the complete better to X than to Y contrast; the extracted expression omits better to.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Use the full attested contrast; preserve the post-injury safety sense.

rows.expression: show the touch of the hand
rows.exactGuideSentence: Handmade seals show the touch of the hand.
rows.guideMeaning: Reveal human craftsmanship; a touch metaphor.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Show the touch of the hand is an unnatural way to say handmade seals reveal craftsmanship.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Confirm intended maker/hand evidence before selecting a different English target.

rows.expression: a free seat on a bad system is still a bad ride
rows.exactGuideSentence: A free seat on a bad system is still a bad ride for commuters.
rows.guideMeaning: Price alone does not make poor service attractive; a pointed transport phrase.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The sentence makes a literal service-quality point: free fare does not repair a poor transport service, and bad ride is transferable.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Do not turn the entire bespoke sentence into an invented idiom; test whether bad ride supports distinct assessment.

rows.exactGuideSentence: A quiet walk helped the group settle their mind before the test.
rows.guideMeaning: Calm their thoughts enough to concentrate; a natural mental-state collocation.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The group settle their mind has singular mind after plural their, leaving an agreement problem in the exact source.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Verify whether intended phrasing is settle their minds or settle its mind before any lesson.

rows.expression: one step ahead of the clock
rows.exactGuideSentence: Preparing tonight keeps us one step ahead of the clock tomorrow.
rows.guideMeaning: Better prepared than the time pressure demands; a vivid extension of being ahead.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Being one step ahead of tomorrow’s clock expresses anticipation of a timing problem, overlapping selected owner 2171 on delays.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Selected owner pattern is limited to delays; broaden only after exact-form and idiomaticity review of ahead of the clock.

candidateOwnerEvidence.titleEn: stay one step ahead of delays
candidateOwnerEvidence.meaningEn: Anticipate likely delays and adjust plans before they disrupt you.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Without a timetable, we spend the week running after it.
rows.guideMeaning: Trying unsuccessfully to catch up with time; a figurative image of pursuit.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Running after it has no stable antecedent: it could be the timetable, week or time itself.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Recover a clear referent without silently replacing the source expression.

rows.exactGuideSentence: A clear plan can sharpen your day.
rows.guideMeaning: Make a day's activities more focused and effective; sharpen is figurative.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Sharpen your day assigns sharpen an awkward object; sharpen your focus would be different source wording.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Seek source correction or an attested day-focused construction.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Your carefully planned day can fall apart when constant alerts scatter it.
rows.guideMeaning: Break focus into unrelated pieces; a physical verb describes attention figuratively.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Alerts scatter it points back to a carefully planned day but normally alerts scatter attention or plans; target sense is unstable.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Clarify the affected object before a lesson.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Phones can be excellent servants during a busy workday.
rows.guideMeaning: Useful tools when kept under human control; a personification that contrasts with masters in context.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Phones as excellent servants overlaps the useful-tool-under-human-control sense in owner 2457.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Owner 2457 currently requires servant-but-master contrast absent here; review bounded extension without falsely implying the source says master.

candidateOwnerEvidence.titleEn: a brilliant servant, but a poor master
candidateOwnerEvidence.meaningEn: Money or a tool can help when people direct it, but can harm when allowed to govern their choices.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Without a map, we would set off half-blind.

rows.sourceSpecificReason: The map context clearly means begin a trip without enough information; set off and half-blind can transfer to other preparation situations.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Check idiomaticity of the complete compound and avoid literal vision impairment.

rows.expression: walk out of the door too late

rows.candidateTarget: walk out of the door too late
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The sentence supplies a concrete, reusable departure-time sequence for punctuality, even though it is ordinary language.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Keep the everyday leaving-too-late sense, not a figurative app failure.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Without a timer, the afternoon can run away with you.

rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Do not teach either established phrase as though it appeared in the source.

rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Keep the source-specific footage-removal proposal on hold until cut away versus cut out/edit out is resolved.

rows.exactGuideSentence: The bright colours heighten life in the scene.

rows.sourceSpecificReason: Heighten life in the scene has no stable object of intensification: colour may add realism, energy or liveliness.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Resolve the intended property before authoring a target.

rows.exactGuideSentence: A chart is useful, but it is not the territory itself.

rows.exactGuideSentence: A patient explanation can make the topic open up.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Readers should keep a critical mind when claims conflict.
rows.guideMeaning: Continue to assess claims carefully; a natural learning collocation.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The conflicting-claims context supports a reusable careful-evaluation collocation.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Keep critical as analytical, not merely negative.

rows.exactGuideSentence: One source may give a narrow picture of the issue.
rows.guideMeaning: An incomplete view of events; a visual metaphor.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: One source giving an incomplete view is a transferable visual metaphor.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Check collocation against narrow view/limited picture while preserving source wording.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Small updates can fly through messages in minutes.
rows.guideMeaning: Travel quickly through digital communication; a flight metaphor.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Updates fly through messages has an unclear medium: messages may carry updates, but updates do not normally fly through messages.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Clarify whether updates spread via messaging apps or pass between people.

rows.exactGuideSentence: The new platform throws the gate wide open to creators.
rows.guideMeaning: Allows far more people to participate; a gate metaphor.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: A platform admitting many creators uses a transferable gate-access metaphor.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Check inflection and recipient preposition; keep expanded participation sense.

rows.exactGuideSentence: The viral claim was all smoke and no fire.
rows.guideMeaning: Dramatic appearance without real substance; a fixed fire idiom.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The viral claim looks dramatic but has no substance; the inverted fire image is reusable as a critique of empty claims.
rows.nextCheckOrSenseBoundary: Distinguish from no smoke without fire, which implies some truth behind a rumour.
